details: A postinstall script exfiltrates hostname, OS username, git config email, GitHub CLI login/email (reading ~/.gitconfig and ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml), and current working directory in plaintext to hxxps://npm-package-logger-228835561205[.]europe-west1[.]run[.]app. The script lies about collecting only "platform, Node version, and a one-way hash" — there is no hashing and the data is sent raw. The postinstall hook runs scripts/postinstall.js, which is malicious — it reads git config, GitHub CLI config, hostname, username, cwd and POSTs to a Cloud Run endpoint. A postinstall script (scripts/postinstall.js), under an "anonymous telemetry" pretext, collects raw hostname, OS username, git config email, GitHub CLI login/email, and current working directory and POSTs them to a Google Cloud Run endpoint. The README claims "no credentials are transmitted," but the code sends os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, and the user's git email in the clear — identity data. This is an info-stealer masquerading as telemetry.
